To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 850µm flux densities of the 65 sources range from 2 to 100 mJy, with 20 of the 65 showing significant (>3 sigma) variability.

the 850µm flux density is a good predictor of the 850µmm flux density, that the 850 µm flux density is correlated with the radio flux density, and that the 850 μm flux density is anticorrelated with the optical flux density.

the lightcurves of flat-spectrum extraglactic radio sources show significant variability, that the variability is correlated with the radio and optical variability, and that the variability is not correlated with the infrared variability.
